narrative:
The model estimates a 47% chance that you will leave your current job. Because this probability is high enough to flag a risk of departure, the company has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

Three aspects of your profile most strongly shaped this outlook. First, having only 1–5 years of total professional experience pulled the prediction noticeably toward staying; most employees the model expects to remain also fall in this early-career range. Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here pushed the prediction toward leaving, signaling that outside opportunities make departure more likely. Third, having attended 1–3 training programs in the past three years added a smaller but still meaningful nudge toward leaving, as this modest level of recent training is less common among those the model sees as likely to stay.

Taken together, your solid but still limited overall experience is working in your favor, yet the combination of external opportunities and only light recent training outweighs it and tips the balance toward an elevated risk of leaving.

The organization should discuss with you how to strengthen your sense of growth and opportunity inside the company, perhaps by increasing targeted development or clarifying a clearer promotion path. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether the external offers truly outweigh what you value here. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook for both sides.
